sub_question: Determine the first term start year for each legislator.
sub_sql:
SELECT lt.id_bioguide,
       strftime('%Y', MIN(lt.term_start)) AS first_term_start_year
FROM legislators_terms lt
GROUP BY lt.id_bioguide

sub_question: Check whether each legislator is serving on December 31 of the start year (0 years).
sub_sql:
WITH base AS (
    SELECT lt.id_bioguide,
           strftime('%Y', MIN(lt.term_start)) AS first_term_start_year
    FROM legislators_terms lt
    GROUP BY lt.id_bioguide
)
SELECT b.id_bioguide,
       CASE WHEN MAX(CASE WHEN date(b.first_term_start_year || '-12-31') BETWEEN date(lt.term_start) AND date(lt.term_end) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS serving_on_dec31_start_year
FROM base b
JOIN legislators_terms lt ON lt.id_bioguide = b.id_bioguide
GROUP BY b.id_bioguide;

sub_question: Check whether each legislator is serving on December 31 of the year two years after the start year.
sub_sql:
WITH base AS (
    SELECT lt.id_bioguide,
           strftime('%Y', MIN(lt.term_start)) AS first_term_start_year
    FROM legislators_terms lt
    GROUP BY lt.id_bioguide
)
SELECT b.id_bioguide,
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM legislators_terms lt
           WHERE lt.id_bioguide = b.id_bioguide
             AND date((CAST(b.first_term_start_year AS INTEGER) + 2) || '-12-31') BETWEEN date(lt.term_start) AND date(lt.term_end)
       ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS serving_on_dec31_two_years_after_start
FROM base b;

sub_question: Check whether each legislator is serving on December 31 of the year four years after the start year.
sub_sql:
WITH first_start AS (
    SELECT id_bioguide,
           MIN(term_start) AS first_term_start
    FROM legislators_terms
    GROUP BY id_bioguide
), target_dates AS (
    SELECT id_bioguide,
           date((CAST(strftime('%Y', first_term_start) AS INTEGER) + 4) || '-12-31') AS target_date
    FROM first_start
)
SELECT td.id_bioguide,
       CASE WHEN EXISTS (
           SELECT 1
           FROM legislators_terms lt
           WHERE lt.id_bioguide = td.id_bioguide
             AND date(td.target_date) BETWEEN date(lt.term_start) AND date(lt.term_end)
       ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS serving_on_dec31_four_years_after_start
FROM target_dates td;

sub_question: For each state and gender, calculate the proportion of legislators retained at the start year.
sub_sql:
WITH start_year AS (
    SELECT MIN(term_start) AS start_date
    FROM legislators_terms
)
SELECT lt.state,
       l.gender,
       CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN date(lt.term_start) <= date(s.start_date) AND date(lt.term_end) >= date(s.start_date) THEN lt.id_bioguide END) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT lt.id_bioguide) AS proportion
FROM legislators_terms lt
JOIN legislators l ON lt.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
CROSS JOIN start_year s
GROUP BY lt.state, l.gender;

sub_question: For each state and gender, calculate the proportion of legislators retained at year two.
sub_sql:
WITH first_terms AS (
    SELECT lt.id_bioguide,
           MIN(date(lt.term_start)) AS start_date,
           MIN(lt.state) AS state
    FROM legislators_terms lt
    GROUP BY lt.id_bioguide
), retained AS (
    SELECT ft.id_bioguide,
           CASE WHEN EXISTS (
               SELECT 1
               FROM legislators_terms lt2
               WHERE lt2.id_bioguide = ft.id_bioguide
                 AND date(lt2.term_start) <= date(ft.start_date, '+2 years')
                 AND date(lt2.term_end) >= date(ft.start_date, '+2 years')
           ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_retained
    FROM first_terms ft
)
SELECT ft.state,
       l.gender,
       CAST(SUM(r.is_retained) AS REAL) / COUNT(*) AS proportion
FROM first_terms ft
JOIN legislators l ON ft.id_bioguide = l.id_bioguide
JOIN retained r ON ft.id_bioguide = r.id_bioguide
GROUP BY ft.state, l.gender;
critic_feedback: The query calculates a single global 'year_two_date' based on the earliest term_start across all legislators, which does not reflect a per-legislator two‑year retention window required by the sub‑task.; Using the SQLite‑specific DATE function (date(start_date, '+2 years')) may not be valid in the target database environment, leading to potential syntax/runtime errors.; Retention logic should compare each legislator's own start date plus two years, not a global date, to correctly compute the proportion retained at year two for each state and gender.
